name: Bosch EDC16U34 (VAG 1.9 / 2.0 TDI PD)

read_methods.notes: Full read over OBD/CAN per OpenTune's bosch-edc16u34 definition (some cars answer KWP2000, others UDS). Diag-Prof lists a 512 KiB processor area plus 2 MiB external flash. Bench over K-line; ecupinouts notes some bench tools also drive two auxiliary programming-mode lines (GPT1/GPT2). No serial boot mode is documented in the cited sources.

notes: Second-generation VAG unit-injector (PD) diesel ECU, roughly 2004-2009 (Golf V, Touran, A3 8P, Octavia II, Leon II). Part number shown is the VAG prefix (03G906xxx). EDC16U31 shares the same vehicle-side pin assignment per Diag-Prof.

connectors.name: T94

bench.notes: +12 V to T94-18 (terminal 30) and T94-5 (terminal 15), ground T94-1. K-line on T94-72 is the usual bench path; CAN is on T94-89/66.
bench.resistor_notes: If you use CAN on the bench, make sure the bus is terminated (about 60 ohm across CAN-H/CAN-L).

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.
